# How many people attend our classes and performances?

Total attendance across classes, performances/events, and community gatherings, by fiscal
year, with what those attendees paid in tickets and class fees. Attendance counts people —
each registration's ticket records — rather than registration counts (about 1.7 people per
registration); the fiscal year runs July–June and is labeled by its ending year. See
[Methodology](99-methodology.html) for the event categories, the headcount definition, and
the cross-cutting fundraiser / youth / film flags. Class-taking households specifically
are profiled in [Who takes classes at Hubbard Hall?](09-classes.html).

```{python}
#| label: setup-attendance
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from hh.io import read_parquet
from hh.viz import style, BLUE

regs = read_parquet("processed", "registrations_enriched.parquet")

from hh.analytics.attendance import attendance_by_fy
from hh.analytics.mailing import fiscal_year

tab = attendance_by_fy(regs)
current_fy = int(fiscal_year(pd.Series(pd.Timestamp.today()))[0])
complete = tab.loc[tab.index < current_fy]  # the current FY is partial

CATS = ["classes", "performances_events", "community"]
LABEL = {"classes": "Classes", "performances_events": "Performances & events",
         "community": "Community"}
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-attendance-by-fy
attendees = complete[[f"{c}_att" for c in CATS]].astype(int)
attendees["Total"] = attendees.sum(axis=1)
attendees.columns = [*map(LABEL.get, CATS), "Total"]
attendees.index = [f"FY{fy - 2000}" for fy in attendees.index]
attendees.index.name = "Fiscal year"
ytd = int(tab.loc[current_fy, "total_att"])
attendees
```


```{python}
#| label: ytd-note
#| output: asis
#| echo: false
print(f"FY{current_fy - 2000} attendance is year-to-date as of the latest data pull "
      f"and will rise as the year fills out ({ytd:,} attendees so far).")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-attendance-by-fy
#| column: page
long = (complete[[f"{c}_att" for c in CATS]]
        .rename(columns={f"{c}_att": LABEL[c] for c in CATS})
        .reset_index()
        .melt(id_vars="fy", var_name="Category", value_name="Attendees"))
long["FY"] = long["fy"].map(lambda y: f"FY{y - 2000}")
fig = px.bar(long, x="FY", y="Attendees", color="Category",
             category_orders={"Category": [LABEL[c] for c in CATS]},
             color_discrete_sequence=[BLUE, "#b3cde3", "#f0e9d8"])
style(fig).show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-revenue-by-fy
revenue = complete[[f"{c}_rev" for c in CATS]].round(0)
revenue["Total"] = complete["total_rev"].round(0)
revenue.columns = [*map(LABEL.get, CATS), "Total"]
revenue.index = [f"FY{fy - 2000}" for fy in revenue.index]
revenue.index.name = "Fiscal year"
revenue.style.format("${:,.0f}")
```

Notes on these figures:

- **Attendees are people, not registrations** — a family of four on one registration
  counts as four. Only attendees whose ticket status is `SUCCEEDED` are counted, so
  refunded canceled sections contribute nobody.
- **Dollars are registration revenue as recorded in Neon** — ticket and class fees only,
  not donations, and gross: a canceled section keeps its refunded amounts (under $2.5k
  in the latest complete year).
- A small share of attendance (363 attendees and $7,571 in FY26) is booked to Neon's
  internal house accounts — real walk-up tickets, included here but attached to no
  household.
- FY20–FY22 cover the pandemic period and its reopening.
- Events carry cross-cutting flags alongside their category — fundraiser, youth program,
  and film — so, for example, a concert that is also a fundraiser can be counted either
  way; those flags do not change the category totals above.
